paragraphs: The 120d has been a mainstay of the 1 Series diesel range since 2011, spanning two generations under one badge. Early F20/F21 cars (up to 2015) use the N47 — a 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel that became notorious for timing chain guide wear. From 2015, BMW introduced the B47 as a direct replacement, significantly revising the design specifically to address the earlier engine's reputation. The B47 carried over into the F40 generation (2019–2024). Knowing which one your car has matters, because the known wear pattern and rebuild specifics differ between them — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: The 120d is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel fitted to the 120d from 2011 to 2015. This is the engine with the well-documented timing chain guide wear issue — see the callout above. We replace the timing chain, guides and tensioners as standard on every N47 rebuild.

BMW's updated 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel, introduced from 2015 as a significant revision of the N47's design. The timing chain was moved to a more reliable position, and the engine has proven significantly more dependable. We service B47 120d engines to the same high standard as the N47.

compatibility.intro: Because BMW 1 Series 120d can use the N47 or B47 engine code, fitting the wrong replacement risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N47 or B47) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic 120d quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
